text: I sat in the drawing room from four o'clock and heard my husband's will read. I didn't go near the kitchen or the pantry all afternoon. I have staff for that.

assertions.claim: I didn't go into the kitchen or the pantry that afternoon.
assertions.note: She went for her own saccharin, as she does every afternoon, and was too proud to say so.

text: I destroyed the Colonel's medicines myself after he died, as I'm supposed to. I haven't had any digoxin since June. I wasn't in the drawing room; nurses don't sit with the family.

assertions.claim: I haven't had any of the Colonel's digoxin since he died.
assertions.note: She kept the medicines a month longer than she should have, then handed every tablet to the solicitor, and was afraid to admit either.

text: I was in the walled garden from three till five. I never came near the house.

assertions.claim: I was in the garden from three until five.
assertions.note: He went round to the drive to move a car for the wine van, and saw more than he wanted to.

text: I read the will from four o'clock until poor Gerald fell, and I never left the room. I never touched the tea things; Mrs Hobbs did all that. I've never had any of the Colonel's medicines. And the trust accounts, which I have kept for twenty-two years, are in perfect order.

assertions.claim: I never touched the tea things.
I've never had any of the Colonel's medicines.
The trust accounts are in perfect order.
I never left the drawing room during the reading.

text: I didn't get to Ashcombe until half past four. By the time I walked up to the Hall, the doctor's car was already there.

assertions.claim: I didn't reach Ashcombe until half past four.
assertions.note: He came early and hid in the library to hear whether he was in the will. The maid watched him the whole time.
